cohorts.summary: New players face steep hurdles due to sparse tutorials and missing mechanical explanations.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as lacking in thorough tutorials and explanation of crucial mechanics.

citations.review_text: A bit too many mechanics for my taste. I'm still in the tutorial after an hour

If they want me to stick around, they should probably have explained more than five sentences.

Second quest. Have no healing- my mistake, my healer was sabotaging my team and I pulled no other health source. I go into the dungeon. Dismas misses SEVENTEEN CONSECUTIVE ATTACKS.

I'm doing what I can to make sure I'm not blind. I don't know what else to do, because the game only vaguely explains things.

I get that UI is not meant to explain everything- that's fine, but there's a difference between intentionally lacking info, like with the afflictions, and straight up not telling me crucial information

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Early explorers grapple with permanent death, heavy stress management, and harsh resource limits beneath striking atmospheric design.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features permanent character death, meaning heroes who die in dungeons cannot be brought back.

citations.review_text:
Darkest Dungeon is one of those games where no matter how many times you get your butt kicked you keep crawling back to it. Well at least that's how I personally view it. This game is not for the faint of heart. It is brutally difficult. RNG can and WILL screw you over at every opportunity it can get it's grubby fingers on. Auto saves are frequent and so character death and other events can't be save scummed through. 

Your characters can succumb to all manner of nonsense from disease, insanity, heart attack, literally just disappearing from the hamlet if they feel like it under certain circumstances. Gold and supplies are in high demand and every recruit that dies is a sunk cost. So the game is this careful balance of rationing everything with risk around every corner. Awful as it sounds there's something about overcoming the odds that I just find plain satisfying and thus I continue to play. So that begs the question is DD a good game? I would say yes it is, but it's not a game I would recommend to everyone. This game should only really be played by the hardcore crowd. If you like Dark Souls, Etrian Odyssey, Dead Cells maybe, you'll feel right at home here. Otherwise I would tread carefully.   

Still gonna leave a thumbs up all the same, because games like these are rare indeed.

One of the best games I ever played. Very atmospheric. Every dungeon dive feels trepidious since there's permadeath, and the music and voiceover pulls you in. Limited inventory forces you to choose between supplies (safety) and loot (reward). There's no clear-cut choice. Because light and food dwindle over time the further you dungeon dive, it becomes a race to reach your objectives. And on top of all this, you need to manage your heroes' stress. Simply brilliant.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that managing character stress, mental health, and diseases is costly, time-consuming, and can lead to adverse party behaviors.

citations.review_text: Great combat, great aesthetics, overall it's a great experience for fans of anything grimdark or fantasy. It's got a solid gameplay loop and there's a lot of customization for each hero archetype, of which there are many! My only gripes are that some enemies can be annoyingly hard to kill (fuck The Collector) and the mental health/disease mechanics are not only extremely costly, but extremely time consuming to manage. Even if your heroes don't experience mental breaks, trying to keep their stress low without camping is incredibly difficult. But maybe that's a skill issue on my part. Overall, 8/10 experience!

Oh man i love this game, Go into a dungeon, clear it with little work but my adventurer gets an anxiety attack and attacks my thief and freaking murders him in cold blood before dying them selves. Its actually a ton of fun highly reccomend it, unless you have anger issues maybe skip on it if you dont like frustrating situations

citations.review_text: The game relies too heavily on RNG, punishing even the most well made strategy. The difficulty comes from how tedious it is, and the grind, not the actual combat. A waste of a good narrative and beautiful artstyle

Only reason I'm still playing it is because it took 2 hours for me to realize I hated it so I cant refund it.

This game is not for me. It forces me to play in the way I don't like. In other RPG/survival games I usually grind low level dungeons to get enough XP and money and only take higher difficulty dungeons when I feel ready. This game forces me to do higher level dungeons after some time even when my party is rubish. I don't have enough money for rest or to remove negative traits from party members even if I try to grind. After some time high lvl party members refuse to enter low level dungeons because they are "too good". You have very limited number of inventory slots. If you try to prepare and buy a lot of stuff before entering dungeon - it gets wasted because it can't be reused after leaving dungeon or you ran out of space for loot and have to delete it. Items in this game are bad most of them reduce one stat while increasing other. I don't want to use them because ever some best items reduce Speed stat.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the hand-drawn dark art style, atmospheric music, and the voice acting of the narrator.

citations.review_text: Darkest Dungeon is a brutal, super addictive gothic roguelike that turns dungeon crawling into a high stakes battle against both monsters and your own party's sanity. Building out a squad of flawed heroes, managing torchlight in pitch black corridors, and making tough tactical calls during turn based fights keeps you locked in every run. The dark hand drawn art style and iconic narrator give the whole game an unforgettable atmosphere that makes surviving a tough expedition feel incredible.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Mid-game adventurers continue navigating heavy stress systems and unpredictable random outcomes within the distinctive art style.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the art style, atmosphere, and narrator are high quality features of the game.

citations.review_text:
I'm well aware I'm going against the grain on this one, but I will not reccomend this game and I'll try to be fair about why.

First let's talk about some of the good things.
The voice acting and art design are all very very good. The narrator, RIP, is a fucking legend. The game itself, a lovecraftian masterpiece when it comes to enemy and area design.

Okay, the bad now.
Its an RNG heavy game, this is supposed to be part of its charm. Bad luck comes, Bad luck goes. Good luck comes, Good luck goes. But.. there is never good luck. There is neutral luck and then bad luck that practically makes you start over. 

I should like a game like this, but after so many tries and so many times of just getting kicked in the dick.. no. If you like this game? Good, play it and love it. Life is short. I will never reccomend this experience because personally, I think its fatally flawed.

Guess I'm in the minority with an opinion like that.
Amazing atmoshpere and art style. The narrator is superb.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gameplay as heavily reliant on unpredictable random number generation.

citations.review_text:
As an utter beginner in this kind of game it really wasn't as mind boggling difficult as imagined. I was drawn in by the artstyle and stayed for the gameplay. 

- It's not a game for everyone with the rng (random crits galore) but honestly a lot of the issues people mentioned can be negated. Radiant mode saves a lot of unnecessary and repetitive grind while keeping the difficulty mostly the same (well, except for intermediate dungeons those are nerfed to the ground when you can bring higher level heroes in). Ofc it's not the initial "intended" way to play, but it's literally just base game with less "artificial playtime bloat".
- Unless you're going all Leper there's quite a lot of repositioning moves for when the deck gets shuffled.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a stress mechanic that heavily impacts characters during dungeon runs.

citations.review_text: At the time of writing this review, i am still not done with it. It is punishing. It is gory. Your heroes are imperfect, and stress can get the better of them, just like their phobias, aspirations and fears. Some dungeon delving runs wil be doomed. But you will learn. For better of for worse. Venture into the darkest dungeon, and hope that you come out of it sane. And alive, if you're one of the lucky few.

The graphics are great, the difficulty of the game matches the game's themes of despair and desperation quite well... but holy hell is it a slog to play. This game has permadeath and a forced ironman mode, which would both be fine on their own, but luck plays a huge part in this game. A string of bad luck is all you need to suffer a complete party wipe no matter how well you're doing at any point, and even if you don't suffer from that, there's several other things that can keep a hero unusable for quite a while, such as high stress or disease.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term veterans find endgame achievements exceptionally niche and difficult to unlock.

claims.claim: Achievements are criticized as absurdly situational, niche, and difficult to complete.

citations.review_text:
This game is not for everyone. It is very difficult, puts you into unfair situations and will often be frustrating. However, I have grown to love the hardships the game puts you through. You never really fully learned everything there is to know, I also learn new stuff every other time I look something up or find a new interaction and I'd say I've had my fair share of playtime. There is endless ways you can challenge yourself, or choose to be more casual. There is plenty of mods and some settings that will allow for all sorts of simplified, easier, harder or even extended gameplay with new enemies and playable characters. 
If you have been thinking about trying this game, please do give it a genuine shot. Past the first struggles might just be one of your new favorite games, as it was for me.

The only thing i would never recommend is trying to 100% this game, especially when you have the dlcs. Some of the achievements are really f*cking stupid. Please trust me on that, ive been through them all (minus the latest dlc).

And as always:
Remind yourself that overconfidence is a slow and insidious killer.

The narration is very good, the story is interesting, the universe is well crafted and its a great game to lose hours and hours on.

Yet...Yet the RNG is the biggest enemy, forever, it is always teeth chattering infuriating to have something with let's say, more than 80% of chance of defending against something and still get hit with it, even more so if it's a death's door check...My biggest gripe will always be the RNG but since that can't be helped with and its illogical to argue about it, in that case in terms of things i dislike in this game it's that the game is pretty heavy on dlc, which in my opinion is a bad monetization tactic, cant deny they're (in average) good dlcs though, with the last one "The fire's edge" being kinda shite but i digress. Other gripe is the achievements are very situational and clearly the devs didnt intend for people to get them all, some are absurdly niche and others are absurdly hard to do, but that of course is the literal least of our concerns.(i think).

single_points.text: One reviewer says the game is basically unplayable without QOL and rebalancing mods to make it fair.

citation.review_text: Game is basically unplayable without a number of QOL and rebalancing mods to actually make it fair.
